Under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) and the guidance issued by the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH), an AI‑based clinical decision support tool that provides diagnostic or treatment recommendations to clinicians is typically classified as a Software as a Medical Device (SaMD). An AI tool that merely analyzes existing clinical data and does not generate new test results typically falls outside CLIA’s scope, provided it does not constitute a “laboratory test” under 42 U.S.C. § 263a. However, if the software incorporates or generates new biomarker measurements—e.g., by processing raw imaging or genomic data—it may be deemed a laboratory-developed test (LDT) and thus subject to CLIA certification requirements.
